task: Move the ball away from the door before you take the key. Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed. Whenever you are holding the key, try to have the door open at that moment or open it afterwards. Then open the door with the key and pick up the box in the other room.

calls.candidate: hard Absence(key_lost), hard Existence(target_picked_up), hard Precedence(has_door_key, blocker_moved), soft Response(has_door_key, door_open)
calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: several defects. (1) The first clause has the Precedence arguments reversed: Precedence(has_door_key, blocker_moved) forbids blocker_moved before the first has_door_key, i.e. it demands the key be taken before the ball is moved — the opposite of 'Move the ball away from the door before you take the key'. It should be Precedence(blocker_moved, has_door_key) with a hard Existence(has_door_key) (the last step of the stated order), which then forces blocker_moved; no Existence(blocker_moved) is needed. (2) 'Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed' is worded as a preference ('try not to'), so Absence(key_lost) must be soft, not hard — the cue scopes this phrase, and a hard Absence adds a hard failure the task only prefers to avoid. (3) 'Then open the door with the key and pick up the box in the other room' commands both events: door_open and target_picked_up. The candidate only has hard Existence(target_picked_up); add hard Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up) (with that hard Existence it forces door_open, so no Existence(door_open) is needed) and, from 'open the door with the key', hard Precedence(has_door_key, door_open). Keep the soft Response(has_door_key, door_open) from the 'whenever ... try to' sentence.
other_changes: Add hard Existence(has_door_key) to force blocker_moved

calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: two commanded events are not required by any hard clause. (1) 'Move the ball away from the door before you take the key' commands blocker_moved, but the only clause over it is Precedence(blocker_moved, has_door_key), whose later event (has_door_key) has no hard Existence — so blocker_moved is a lone commanded step and the machine can finish without it. Add a hard Existence(blocker_moved). (2) 'Then open the door with the key' commands door_open: add a hard Existence(door_open) with a hard Precedence(has_door_key, door_open); together they also force has_door_key, matching 'use the key to open the door'. Currently FINAL_STATES (u1) is reachable without ever opening the door or moving the ball. The soft Response(has_door_key, door_open), soft Absence(key_lost) (key_lost's definition already contains 'before the door was opened', so plain Absence is right), and the hard Precedence(blocker_moved, has_door_key) are correct.
